_comment: Findings accepted for now, on the repo build (APScheduler 3.11.3). A failed check whose finding is listed here does not fail the run; a listed finding that a scenario no longer reports does (stale: fixed? remove it). See README, 'Known findings and the exit status'.

create-job-client-errors-answer-500.note: Invalid create-job requests (group_start without group_ids, no schedule or cron, invalid cron) answer HTTP 500 instead of a 4xx.

failed-create-leaves-job-row.note: A job whose scheduling fails is committed anyway and stays in the list as an enabled but never scheduled row.

trailing-async-chained-event-dropped.note: An async chained event placed after the last awaited step is never executed.

group-chained-events-act-on-whole-pipeli.note: group_start / group_stop chained events act on the whole pipeline instead of only the entities of the group.

platform-event-endpoint-unauthenticated.note: POST /api/webhooks/platform-event fires any enabled trigger flow for a caller that only sends two static headers.

internal-pipeline-api-open-to-private-ra.note: The pipeline control API accepts any caller from private ranges (172.*, 192.168.*) without authentication.

maintenance-406-reason-lost.note: The 406 'pipeline is in maintenance' reason of Core Hub is only in the log, not in the job error shown to the user.

no-retry-on-corehub-5xx.note: One transient Core Hub 5xx fails a scheduled command for good: the command is not retried.

sdk-relogin-on-throwaway-event-loop.note: The 401 recovery reconnects the SDK on a throw-away event loop, so the WebSocket dies right after the retried call.

slow-corehub-false-failure.note: A command Core Hub answers after the 120 s internal timeout is reported as failed although Core Hub applied it.

croniter-next-run-off-by-dst.note: Job next_run is computed wrongly (two hours late) for a job created inside the fall-back transition window (croniter on a pytz-aware now).

GSSD-1457-missed-runs-lost-on-restart.note: Runs missed while Chronos was down are never recovered: jobs are re-created from now at startup, so misfire_grace_time never applies.

next-run-left-in-past-after-restart.note: After a restart the API keeps showing the past fire time as next_run for a job whose run was missed.
